study_design: Clinic-based case-control study of newly diagnosed prostate cancer cases and cancer-free controls
reason: The study evaluates newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed prostate cancer overall. No aggressive disease definition or aggressive incident analysis is reported. The total sample size is not explicitly stated and was not inferred by summing cases and controls.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: High whole-blood oleic acid composition (tertile 3 vs. tertile 1: OR, 0.37; CI, 0.14-0.0.98) and moderate palmitic acid proportions (tertile 2: OR, 0.29; CI, 0.12-0.70) (tertile 3: OR, 0.53; CI, 0.19-1.54) were inversely related to risk of PCa, whereas men with high linolenic acid proportions were at increased likelihood of PCa (tertile 3 vs. tertile 1: OR, 2.06; 1.29-3.27).
estimate_classifications.reason: The row is for whole-blood oleic acid and overall prostate cancer. The abstract does not define the outcome as aggressive.

additional_estimates.comparison: Highest versus lowest tertile of dietary MUFA intake
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: Higher intakes of dietary MUFA were inversely related to prostate cancer (tertile 3 vs. tertile 1: OR, 0.39; CI 0.16-0.92).
additional_estimates.count_excerpt: Case-control study of 209 men 40-80 years old with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed prostate cancer and 226 cancer-free men attending the same urology clinics.
additional_estimates.endpoint_definition: Newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed prostate cancer
